tagline.text: The first town of Eastern Visayas, a historic town in northern Leyte on Carigara Bay

location.label: Location
location.text: Northern Leyte Island, a first-class municipality on Carigara Bay

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,500 (per person, based on a round-trip day trip from Tacloban or Ormoc including transport and meals)

children.text: Carigara is a town in northern Leyte founded on January 25, 1571 and called the first town of Eastern Visayas. In half a day you can see Holy Cross Church, the Datu Gara shrine, the migratory bird wetlands of Carigara Bay and local treats such as pastillas and humba.

Carigara is a first-class municipality in northern Leyte on Carigara Bay, surrounded by rice fields and mountains. It borders Capoocan to the west, Ormoc to the south, Jaro to the southeast, Tunga to the east and Barugo to the northeast. According to Wikipedia its area is 117.86 square kilometers, its 2024 population is 56,060 and it has 49 barangays. The highest point is 1,267 m and the town center averages about 130 m above sea level. Waray is the most widely spoken language, with a minority speaking Cebuano and Tagalog, and most residents are Christian. The economy centers on farming, with rice, root crops, bananas, coconuts, mangoes and vegetables. Wikipedia gives no distances to Tacloban or Ormoc, and on a map the straight-line distance is said to be about 35 km to Tacloban and about 34 km to Ormoc. The road distance is longer, so check locally. In 2024 the municipality's revenue was about ₱249.3 million, and poverty incidence fell from 43.75 percent in 2000 to 29.57 percent in 2023. Today it is a quiet provincial town sustained by farming and small-scale commerce.

Its history goes back before the Spanish era. Carigara is said to have been founded on January 25, 1571 and is described as the first town established in Eastern Visayas. The name evolved from "Kan Gara" to Kalgara and then to Carigara after the Spanish arrived, and legend names Datu Gara, who came from Borneo, as its founder. The Jesuits, led by Fr. Pedro Chirino, arrived on July 16, 1595. When Leyte and Samar were separated from Cebu province in 1735, Carigara served for a time as the provincial capital. Walking through the town you can see pride in being "first in Eastern Visayas" everywhere, shown in the Datu Gara shrine and the Heroes Shrine.

Holy Cross Parish Church (in Barangay Ponong) in the town center is described as the oldest and largest church in Carigara. One guide says it was established in 1595 and is the oldest parish in Leyte, but another source says only that it is the oldest and largest church in Carigara, so it is wiser not to state it as certain. Wikipedia's list of attractions also includes St. Francis of Assisi Parish in Barangay Jugaban. Plaza Triunfo, near the church, is the town's largest plaza, and the big town fiesta is held every July 16 for the Feast of the Triumph of the Holy Cross. On July 14, 2018 about 9,642 people danced the Kuratsa in an attempt at a Guinness record, but it was not certified. The Magara Festival was first held on January 25, 2019 to celebrate agriculture, local products and heritage, and the festival dates vary between sources, so confirm them locally.

The food and scenery are also worth a look. Carigara is known for pastillas, humba and hubhob, a dessert of grated cassava, eggs, kalamay, milk and sugar cooked in bamboo over charcoal. Lauron's Boulevard, a street food strip across Barangays Baybay and Ponong, serves isaw and pork barbecue. The Carigara Bay wetlands are recorded as a stop for egrets, the Philippine duck, plovers and sandpipers on the East Asian–Australasian Flyway, and the DENR has named the wetlands of Carigara Bay and Ormoc Bay the most frequently visited habitats for migratory birds in Eastern Visayas. Some travel writers say the sunset over Carigara Bay can rival those of Bali and Manila Bay on a clear day. Every Black Saturday there are Turugpo duels between two male carabaos or two male horses, and every year barangays and agencies compete with decorated arches in the Kalsada ni Gara street decoration contest. Cassidy Elementary School (in Barangay Ponong) is known for its classical-style building, and the Kan Gara Gymnasium is the town's largest. Travel site listings also include the Carigara Tide Embankment and the public market, but little detail is available.
The town's main church in Barangay Ponong. Some guides say it was established in 1595 and is the oldest parish in Leyte, but sources differ. Visit quietly during Mass.
The town's largest plaza and the center of festivals. Events are said to continue for nearly a month around the July 16 Feast of the Triumph of the Holy Cross.

blocks.title: Datu Gara shrine and Heroes Shrine

children.text: A shrine honoring the legendary founder Datu Gara is in Barangay Canal, and the Heroes Shrine stands between Barangays Baybay and Ponong. They are places that show the town's pride.
The municipal library and museum in Barangay Baybay. You can see local history and materials, but check opening hours locally.
Barangay Jugaban has houses more than a century old, and Gawas an Harigue in Baybay is an old house with exposed posts. The Lumen Ancestral House (Barangay Sawang) is said to shelter swiftlets.

An annual street decoration contest in which barangays and agencies build decorated arches, with lit-up streets at night as the highlight. The timing is tied to the festival, so check with the municipal office.
A food street where people gather in the evening. You can try street food such as isaw and pork barbecue, and ask the price first.
A coastal wetland that migratory birds visit. Early morning is best for watching birds, and you should ask the municipal or environment office how to get access.

Vans, jeepneys and buses connect Tacloban to Carigara. On November 24, 2021 the municipality is said to have assigned new modernized PUVs to the Tacloban–Carigara route, but you need to check current routes and fares at the local terminal.
Vans and buses to Carigara also run from Ormoc. Check distance and travel time at the terminal.
Guides say few bus companies are based in Carigara.
Pedicabs are common in town, and tricycles and habal-habals serve outlying barangays.
The port on Carigara Bay is in Barangay Baybay.

Carigara is comfortable for walking and outdoor activity in the dry season from December to May. The big festival is the July 16 Feast of the Triumph of the Holy Cross, so July is lively even when it rains.

According to modeled climate data, annual rainfall is about 1,509 mm, with February the driest month and June to October the wettest. Average daily highs are about 30°C and lows about 24°C, with about 265 rainy days a year. This is modeled data, so check the actual weather before you go.

Carigara town has small hotels, and Wikivoyage lists Hotel Baudilio, but the information is old. Most travelers make a round-trip day visit from Tacloban or Ormoc. Check lodging directly on arrival.

Carigara's signature foods are pastillas (a milk candy sweet), humba (braised pork) and hubhob (a cassava dessert cooked in bamboo). Wikivoyage lists a restaurant called Balai Constancia, but that is a 2016 listing, so check whether it still operates. Street food is easiest to find on Lauron's Boulevard.

The only public hospital in town is the Carigara District Hospital, electricity is supplied by the LEYECO 3 cooperative and water by the Metro Carigara Water District. Higher-education institutions include the Carigara campus of Eastern Visayas State University and Holy Cross College. Telecom service comes from Smart, Globe, Dito and others, and satellite and cable TV are said to be available. The town has about 30 elementary schools and 6 high schools, with Carigara National High School and Carigara National Vocational School the best known.
Hotels and transport get crowded in festival season (mid-July). Arrive early.
Migratory birds are best seen on the shore in the early morning. Ask the local office how to get access.
For street food, ask the price first and check hygiene with your own eyes before eating.
Check the time of the last transport back on the way in.

Turugpo (duels between male carabaos or horses) is said to be held on Black Saturday, but because it is an event where animals fight each other, check the local rules and decide for yourself whether to watch.
Festival dates differ between sources, so check the municipality's official website.
This is a town with little information available. Check opening hours and fees locally and leave some slack in your schedule.
The founding year of Holy Cross Church and the claim that it is the "oldest" differ between sources and cannot be stated as certain.
